'''Janice B. Spofford''' (November 1925 – March 2018) was an American [[Evolutionary biology|evolutionary biologist]] and [[geneticist]] who taught at the [[University of Chicago]] for decades starting in 1949, retiring at the rank of associate professor emeritus in the Department of Ecology and Evolution. She served as president of the [[American Society of Naturalists]] in 1979. 

== Life and career ==
Spofford was born Janice Brogue on November 14, 1925, in [[Chicago]], [[Illinois]], where she would live her entire life except for a brief residency in [[Mason City, Iowa|Mason City]], [[Iowa]], as a child. She graduated from [[Hyde Park Academy High School|Hyde Park High School]] and received a scholarship to attend the [[University of Chicago]] by earning the top score in a statewide Latin competition. She received her [[Bachelor of Philosophy|PhB]] in 1944, [[Bachelor of Science|SB]] in 1946, and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in 1955, all from the University of Chicago.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Peart |first=Andrew |date=Fall 2018 |title=University obituaries |url=https://mag.uchicago.edu/university-news/university-obituaries-34 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250618091840/https://mag.uchicago.edu/university-news/university-obituaries-34 |archive-date=2025-06-18 |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=University of Chicago Magazine |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Bevington |first=David |date=March 27, 2018 |title=Janice Spofford, evolutionary biologist and lifelong Hyde Parker, 1925 to 2018 |url=https://emeritifaculty.uchicago.edu/news-announcements/article/janice-spofford-1925-2018/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251224005015/https://emeritifaculty.uchicago.edu/news-announcements/article/janice-spofford-1925-2018/ |archive-date=2025-12-24 |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=University of Chicago Office of the Provost - Emeriti Faculty}}</ref> Her dissertation as submitted to the Department in Zoology was "The Relation between Expressivity and Selection against Eyeless in ''[[Drosophila melanogaster|Drosophila Malanogaster]]''."<ref>Janice B. Spofford (1955), ''The Relation between Expressivity and Selection against Eyeless in Drosophila Malanogaster'', PhD dissertation, University of Chicago, https://www.proquest.com/docview/301995294</ref>

In 1949 at age 23, Spofford began teaching biology at UChicago, where she was the university's youngest faculty member. She spent her entire academic career at UChicago, researching topics such as fruit fly genetics (''[[Drosophila melanogaster|Drosophila]]'' ''[[Drosophila melanogaster|melanogaster]]'') and the phenomenon of [[heterosis]]. She served as an associate member of UChicago's Committee on Evolutionary Biology and the Committee on Genetics, Genomics, and Systems Biology. She retired at the rank of associate professor emeritus in the Department of Ecology and Evolution.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> She served as president of the [[American Society of Naturalists]] in 1979 after serving as secretary from 1971 to 1973.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Past Officers of the ASN |url=https://www.amnat.org/about/history/past-ec.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250531112119/https://www.amnat.org/about/history/past-ec.html |archive-date=2025-05-31 |access-date=2025-12-24 |website=[[American Society of Naturalists]] |language=en}}</ref> Spofford published research and review articles in ''[[The American Naturalist]]'', [[Genetics (journal)|''Genetics'']], ''[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]]'', ''[[Genetics Research]]'', [[Developmental Biology (journal)|''Developmental Biology'']], ''[[Heredity (journal)|Heredity]]'', ''[[Science (journal)|Science]]'', ''[[Brookhaven National Laboratory|Brookhaven Symposia in Biology]]'', and other scientific journals.

She was married to Richardson L. Spofford, an accountant. They had two sons. She died in late March 2018 at the age of 92.<ref name=":0" />
